ABW.name: Activity-Based Working
ABW.description: Employees move between different zone types based on the task at hand rather than occupying assigned desks.
ABW.spaceReduction: Reduces workstations needed by 20–30% vs traditional assigned seating
ABW.bestFor: Knowledge workers, professional services, creative agencies, tech companies

hybridModel.name: Hybrid Work Layout
hybridModel.description: Designed for 2–3 days in-office attendance. Higher collaboration-to-focus ratio than traditional offices.
hybridModel.note: Pre-2020 models were the inverse — 60% individual desks, 20% meeting rooms, 20% other

traditional.name: Traditional Assigned Seating
traditional.description: Each employee has an assigned desk. Standard for law firms, government, financial services.
traditional.bestFor: Law firms, regulated industries, finance, government

executiveOffices.furnitureSpec: Executive L-desk or straight desk, executive chair, 2–4 visitor chairs, credenza, bookshelf
executiveOffices.designNote: Private, acoustically treated. Premium finish and material specification.

openPlanWorkstations.furnitureSpec: Desk, task chair, screen divider, mobile pedestal, cable management
openPlanWorkstations.densityTip: Allow 1.2–1.5m aisle between back-to-back rows minimum

ratios.50_100staff: 1 boardroom (16–20 seats) + 4–6 meeting rooms mixed size
ratios.100plus: Multiple boardrooms + tiered meeting room system

boardroomMeetingRooms.furnitureSpec: Conference table, executive chairs, AV credenza, whiteboard wall or screen

receptionWaiting.furnitureSpec: Reception station, lounge seating (2–8 seats depending on traffic), coffee table, feature lighting, occasional table
receptionWaiting.designPriority: Highest ROI per square metre — invest disproportionately here

breakoutSocial.furnitureSpec: Modular lounge seating, high tables with stools, soft seating clusters, kitchen/café furniture
breakoutSocial.businessCase: 20%+ higher engagement scores in offices with quality social spaces — position as talent attraction investment

focusRooms.description: Small 1–4 person spaces for focused work, calls, or sensitive conversations
focusRooms.recommendationRule: Every open-plan office above 20 staff needs at least 1 acoustic pod or phone booth

spacePlanningRules.circulationBuffer: Always add 15–20% to furniture footprint for circulation paths
spacePlanningRules.egressRequirements: 1.2m minimum aisle width for fire egress compliance (AS/NZS 1428)
spacePlanningRules.acousticZoning: Separate noisy collaboration areas from quiet focus zones with at least one acoustic barrier
spacePlanningRules.naturalLight: Workstations should face the window or be perpendicular — never back to window, never facing into glare
spacePlanningRules.biophilicElements: Plants, natural materials, timber tones — documented 15% productivity improvement. Recommend where possible without cost premium.
spacePlanningRules.receptionVisibility: Reception should be the first thing visitors see from the lift lobby — orientation and first impression matter
